newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps broadly steady, bar stronger mogas.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps broadly steady, bar stronger mogas.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to a touch firmer on Wednesday, except for stronger gasoline as crude futures consolidated after Monday's firmer close.
Brent crude CFDs were unchanged close in and stronger further out, fuel ticked up 50 cents or so and gasoline was $1-2.00 firmer. Naphtha was marginally stronger.
Dealers said the continued lack of resolution to the timetable of Iraqi exports which are now not expected before August, has given the market a more bullish tinge.
Brent CFDs for July 23-25 were pegged steady at +10 cents against September Brent from +11 cents while July 28-August 1 CFDs hovered around +7 cents against September from +6 cents.
Further out stronger gains were seen with August 4-8 moving to -5/4 cents against September from -10 cents with August 11-15 firming to -12/13 cents from -17/18 cents.
Heavy fuel was a touch firmer with August swaps put around $89.50. Physical barges were done at $89.50 fob a couple of times with $90.00 also trading twice.
August gasoline was around $191.00, up from $189 while September remained backwardated by $4, valued at $187.00. October's backwardation to September held steady at $5.
Naphtha was broadly unchanged to marginally firmer by 25-50 cents. August was put at $185 with September at $183.75.
Gas oil crack spreads for 4Q were pegged around $4.30, 1Q98 at $.40 and 2Q98 at $4.00.
